The scheduled run's Slack report is a thread per pair and eval config: a message about the arm, and the numbers behind it in replies.

The message answers "is this arm healthy, and what did it cost?". A grid cell carries the reward's coloured band, the reward, and in italics what the trial's workspace agent spent and how long its conversation took (`$1.23 9m05s`) -- `$12.50+` where the figure is a floor, `$?` where a model it ran on carries no price, `<$0.01` for real money too small to show, and nothing where the trial recorded no spend. The pair's line carries the message's own spend, in the wording the run's markdown summary uses (`agent spend $23.68+ over 2 trials, 1 unknown; harness spend $0.35 over 2 trials`). Every grid column is left-aligned, and the legend under it explains the italic figures and both marks.

The first reply holds every scoring input behind that grid, as two tables -- `outcome` and `quality`, then `harness_quality` and `gates` -- with one row per graded trial, or per step of a stepped one, and each dimension a bold super-column carrying its own score over the criteria that make it up, programmatic checks and judges alike. A gate reads as a check mark or the red `:x:` rather than as a number. A table holds only the trials scored on its own two dimensions, so a trial the other table measured is absent rather than drawn as a row of dashes. The message carries no judge-scores container; the reply is where the scores are.

The second reply holds the diagnostics detail: the known failures, the facts an agent did not follow, and the live invariants each cell's trials missed. The message's details block keeps the statuses, the diagnostics that measured nothing, the unsupported behaviour cells, an uncovered pass's failures and the unconfirmed models.

`minds-evals post-slack-report --payloads <file> --channel <C-id>` posts the report. It posts as the app whose bot token is in `SLACK_MINDS_EVALS_BOT_TOKEN`, which is what makes the replies threadable, and falls back to the incoming webhook in `SLACK_MINDS_EVALS_WEBHOOK`, which cannot thread and so gets the top messages alone. With neither it warns and posts nothing. The app behind the token needs `chat:write`, `chat:write.customize` for the name and avatar every message posts under, and membership of the channel. A refusal is always a warning: a message whose blocks Slack will not render is reposted as its own text, a thread Slack refuses costs the next one nothing, and the exit code is zero once posting has begun. A rate-limited message is posted again after the `Retry-After` Slack named -- a second where it named none, thirty at the most -- for up to three attempts before it is warned about like any other refusal. A message whose plain text runs past the 40,000 characters Slack takes -- a wide suite's scoring fence does -- is cut on a line boundary as it goes out and ends in a line saying so, with the whole of it in the run summary.

`minds-evals ci-report --output` writes a JSON array of `{message, replies}` objects, one per thread, which is the file `post-slack-report` reads.
